eips.title: Hardware and Bandwidth Recommendations
eips.summary: Discussed updating recommended hardware specs, particularly raising sequential read/write speeds from 500 to 1000–2000 MB/s for Glamsterdam.

moments.context: Jochem introduced EIP-7870 as needing an update because current 500 MB/s sequential speeds are too low for Glamsterdam worst-case blocks, which take 8 seconds on such hardware.
Discussion on whether to update this living EIP or create a new per-fork EIP; consensus leaned toward keeping it as one living document.
Dustin pushed back on the narrative that specs are generally too low, noting that memory and CPU requirements already seem high, though he stipulated disk speed claims may be valid.
Jochem argued for per-fork EIPs for clearer communication; Łukasz disagreed, preferring a single EIP with history to avoid confusion from multiple documents.

eips.title: Fork-choice enforced Inclusion Lists (FOCIL)
eips.summary: Included in the proposed heze-devnet-2 EIP list; interactions with frames noted as key reason to merge CL and EL devnets.

moments.context: Listed as one of the EIPs for the next CL devnet alongside EIP-8015, EIP-8365, and EIP-8198.
Justin Florentine noted FOCIL and frames interactions as a reason to get them on a combined devnet quickly, since interactions could impact capacity.

eips.title: Remove `deposit` and `eth1data` fields
eips.summary: Included in the proposed heze-devnet-2 as one of the CFI'd CL EIPs to remove deposit and eth1data fields.

moments.context: Listed by Jun Song and Spencer as part of the heze-devnet-2 scope along with EIP-7805, EIP-8365, and EIP-8198.
Matthew Keil confirmed support for including the ETH1 data removal alongside FOCIL and 0x00 validator changes.

eips.title: Disallow new 0x00 validators
eips.summary: Included in proposed heze-devnet-2 to disallow new 0x00 validators; no objections raised.

moments.context: Listed as one of the four CL EIPs for the next devnet by Jun Song.
Matthew Keil referenced closing the door to 0x00 validators as part of the devnet scope he supports.

eips.title: Quick Slots
eips.summary: Quick Slots proposed for heze-devnet-2 but with 12-second slot duration initially; shorter slots deferred until more clients are ready.

moments.context: Listed as one of the CFI'd CL EIPs for the next devnet, with the question of whether to use 10s or 12s slot time.
Dustin said Nimbus is not likely to have quick slots ready in this timeframe; agreed to keep 12-second slots for heze-devnet-2.
Justin Traglia proposed merging EIP-8198 into Heze specs as soon as tests pass, with agreement to keep 12s duration for the devnet.
Barnabas said Teku and Lodestar have already implemented even the shorter slots; Jihoon added Lighthouse, giving three clients.

eips.title: EIP Purpose and Guidelines
eips.summary: Referenced in chat regarding the EIP process for modifying living versus final EIPs.

moments.context: Jochem linked EIP-1's process diagram in chat to clarify rules about changing living vs final EIPs, in context of the EIP-7870 update discussion.

eips.title: SETCODEFROM Code Reuse Instruction
eips.summary: Raised repeatedly as a candidate for an upcoming devnet; implemented by two clients and argued as the path to post-quantum migration.

moments.context: CPerezz in chat: "I guess no SETCODEFROM anytime soon… 🙁", reacting to the bogota-devnet-1 scope.
Mario Vega opened the floor on SetCodeFrom, noting strong opinions and mentions in chat.

CPerezz argued the tests exist, Nethermind and Geth have implemented it and pass the EEST PR, it is the main route to early post-quantum migration, and it would let the non-trivial integration with frames be tested.
Toni in chat: "my feeling is do setcodefrom + data repricing"; his consolidated list at 01:05:18 kept set code from first.

eips.title: Frame Transaction
eips.summary: Frame Transaction EIP included in Bogota devnet 1 scope alongside keyed nonces, recent roots, and transaction assertions.

moments.context: Spencer listed EIP-8141 as one of the four EIPs in the Bogota devnet 1 release being prepared for Thursday launch.

eips.title: Keyed Nonces for Frame Transactions
eips.summary: Keyed Nonces for Frame Transactions included in Bogota devnet 1; consensus-breaking interaction with floor gas pricing discussed.

moments.context: Spencer listed EIP-8250 in the Bogota devnet 1 scope.
Toni explained that keyed nonces are part of the transaction envelope and affect floor gas pricing when combined with frames, making it a consensus-breaking change requiring all clients to implement.

eips.title: Recent Roots for Frame Transactions
eips.summary: Recent Roots for Frame Transactions listed as part of Bogota devnet 1 scope.

moments.context: Spencer listed EIP-8272 as one of the four EIPs included in the upcoming Bogota devnet 1 release.

eips.title: Transaction Assertions via State Diff Opcode
eips.summary: Transaction Assertions listed as part of Bogota devnet 1 scope.

moments.context: Spencer listed EIP-7906 (transaction assertions) as the fourth EIP in the Bogota devnet 1 release.

eips.title: Bump nonce of zero-nonce storage accounts
eips.summary: Bump nonce of zero-nonce storage accounts proposed for next devnet; behavior only triggers at fork transition so early testing on multiple devnets is important.

moments.context: Spencer said he and Jochem want EIP-8253 in the next devnet.
Jochem explained the EIP's behavior only happens at the fork transition, so testing it on as many devnets as possible is desirable, and he will open a PR for devnet template accounts.

eips.title: Account Code Restricted ecRecover
eips.summary: Suggested alongside SetCodeFrom as a frames-adjacent EIP to include in an upcoming devnet.

moments.context: Marc suggested SetCodeFrom and EIP-8151 would be cool to go along with frames in a future devnet.

eips.title: State Creation Gas Cost Increase
eips.summary: Toni cited its early inclusion in a previous devnet as a positive precedent for including complex EIPs early.

moments.context: Toni said including EIP-8037 early last time gave time to understand and debug it, and suggested the same approach for data repricing EIPs.

eips.title: Block Access List Byte Floor
eips.summary: Block Access List Byte Floor suggested as a candidate for early devnet inclusion due to its complexity.

moments.context: Toni suggested EIP-8279 as a candidate for early devnet testing since it is the more involved of the data repricing EIPs.
Toni confirmed EIP-8279 would be a candidate for the next devnet based on the principle of adding complex EIPs early.

eips.title: Deactivate SELFDESTRUCT
eips.summary: Maria asked whether deactivating SELFDESTRUCT early would simplify testing; jochem tied it to shipping TCREATE alongside.

moments.context: Maria Silva asked whether adding DEACTIVATE self-destruct earlier would help with testing by removing edge cases; spencer agreed it would.

jochem noted that if deactivate self-destruct ships, EIP-8360 (TCREATE) has to ship too, since patterns using self-destruct get more expensive; Justin Florentine called TCREATE testing orthogonal to Maria's point.
Included in Toni's chat list of candidates for the next devnet: set code from, data repricing, bump nonce, deactivate selfdestruct.

eips.title: TCREATE Opcode
eips.summary: Jochem noted TCREATE must ship alongside deactivate self-destruct to preserve existing patterns, though not necessarily in the same devnet.

moments.context: Jochem said if self-destruct is deactivated, EIP-8360 (TCREATE) must also be included because removing self-destruct eliminates patterns that become more expensive in Glamsterdam; Justin Florentine noted this is orthogonal to testing self-destruct early.
